title: Elimination, Equilibrium, Escape: Cancer Immunoediting vs. Neutral 'Big-Bang' Tumor Evolution and T-Cell Tolerance — How Osias Stutman's leaky athymic nude mice buried cancer immunosurveillance for twenty-five years until Vijay Shankaran and Robert Schreiber's Rag2-/- sarcoma cross-transplants unveiled the Three Es; Catherine Koebel's 200-day occult Equilibrium proof; Nicholas McGranahan and Rachel Rosenthal's TRACERx discoveries of clonal trunk neoantigens, 40% HLA LOH, and epigenetic silencing; Marc Williams and Andrea Sottoriva's 904-tumor 1/f neutral evolution challenge and Gerald Willimsky and Thomas Blankenstein's sporadic tolerogenic oncogene critique; 1/f sequencing-horizon & clonal-ITH math plus immuno-oncology blindspots

teenKit.tldr: Your immune system doesn't just destroy cancer—it acts like an evolutionary personal trainer, accidentally breeding tougher, drug-resistant mutant tumors through a process called Cancer Immunoediting.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how stealthy cancer cells hide from our internal police force is the exact secret behind modern immunotherapy—the breakthrough cancer treatment saving lives today.
keyTakeaways: The Three Es of Immunoediting—Elimination, Equilibrium, and Escape—describe how tumors evolve to outsmart the immune system over time.
A dormant cancer cell can hide invisibly in a healthy human body for 16 years, only to explode into a lethal tumor the moment immune defenses drop.
Not all tumors are aggressively sculpted by the immune system; some expand neutrally while others trick T-cells into total tolerance.

vocab.meaning: The evolutionary process where the immune system destroys weak cancer cells while accidentally selecting and shaping tougher, invisible mutants.
A tense biological standoff where the immune system keeps a hidden tumor completely trapped in check, preventing it from growing or spreading.
Mutated, abnormal proteins on the surface of a cancer cell that act like flashing neon warning signs for the immune system to attack.
A stealth trick where cancer cells delete their molecular ID cards so the immune system's T-cells literally cannot see them anymore.

quiz.question: What happened in the chilling real-life medical case discussed in the episode where a kidney recipient developed fatal melanoma?
options: The patient caught melanoma from a hospital air vent during surgery.
A tiny, dormant cancer cell from a donor who died 16 years earlier woke up when the recipient took immunosuppressive drugs.
The new kidney grew a brand-new type of cancer because of organ rejection.
The patient's own immune system accidentally turned their kidney cells into cancer.
quiz.explanation: Immunosuppressive drugs lowered the patient's defenses, allowing a microscopic, 16-year dormant tumor from the organ donor to explode into a lethal firestorm.

quiz.question: What are the three stages of Cancer Immunoediting in order?
quiz.explanation: The process moves from Elimination (killing most cells), to Equilibrium (a long stalemate), to Escape (tumors breaking free).

quiz.question: Why did early 1970s experiments using 'nude' mice with weak immune systems fail to prove cancer immunosurveillance?
options: The mice were kept in environments too clean to develop spontaneous tumors, and they still had some hidden immune cells left.
The scientists accidentally used human cancer cells instead of mouse cells.
Mice cannot get cancer under any circumstances.
The mice ate a special diet that cured all tumors instantly.
quiz.explanation: The leaky athymic nude mice still possessed residual innate immunity, masking the true power of T-cells until later genetic knockouts proved the theory.
